title: Hetero begins shipping generic HIV prevention drug lenacapavir to Africa
summary: Hetero has initiated phased shipments of generic injectable lenacapavir to Africa, starting with 300,000 vials. The drug, originally developed by Gilead Sciences, is effective for treating multi-drug resistant HIV variants. WHO recommends lenacapavir as a...

contentHtml:
Pharmaceutical company Hetero announced on Thursday that it has commenced phased shipments of generic injectable lenacapavir to Africa, with a planned initial supply of 300,000 vials across Zambia, Uganda and Zimbabwe.

Originally developed by Gilead Sciences, the drug is used in the prevention and treatment of multi-drug resistant variants of HIV, said the company’s statement.

The injectable version of lenacapavir is recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO) as an additional preventative option and has shown efficacy in reducing the risk of HIV acquisition, the release said.

Read more: 18 patent applications for HIV drug lenacapavir may delay affordable generics in India

The company said it expects to introduce its generic oral initiation tablets by January 2027, supporting the complete pre-exposure prophylaxis regimen alongside the injectable formulation.

According to the release, Gilead Sciences had entered into non-exclusive voluntary licensing agreements with six generic manufacturers, enabling the manufacture and supply of the medicine across 120 eligible countries.

Read more: Dr Reddy's inks pact with Gilead for once-yearly HIV prevention drug lenacapavir

The statement said Hetero's generic injectable lenacapavir and oral initiation tablets have received an ERP recommendation, enabling eligible procurement through applicable Global Fund channels, subject to country-level regulatory and procurement requirements.

The pharma company plans to supply generic lenacapavir to 10 additional African countries in early 2027; it also intends to launch the drug in India in the coming months, the release said.
